title: Savings Bonds Pay 5.51%. Here's the Part You Keep.

scenes.vo: A U.S. savings bond pays 5.51 percent. That number won't last.
I bonds pay two rates: a fixed rate locked for life, plus an inflation rate reset every six months.

captions.text: a fixed rate locked for life,
plus an inflation rate reset every six months.

scenes.vo: Right now, that's 1.40 percent fixed, plus about 4.1 from inflation.
Illustrative: 10,000 dollars earns about 275 in six months. You can't cash out for a year.

captions.text: You can't cash out for a year.

scenes.vo: Before buying, check the fixed rate. That's the part you keep.

captions.text: Before buying, check the fixed rate.

composite.unit: % annualized composite rate, I bonds issued Nov 1, 2026 – Apr 30, 2027
composite.source: Tipswatch and Doctor of Credit, both published 2026-10-30; Wolf Street 2026-10-30 (TreasuryDirect rate page blocked to automated access); recomputed with 31 CFR 359.14 in scenes/math.ts

fixed.unit: % fixed rate, established for the life of the bond (31 CFR 359.10)
fixed.source: Same as composite; rule text 31 CFR 359.10 (Cornell LII, retrieved 2026-11-18)

semiannualInflation.unit: % semiannual inflation rate = CPI-U (NSA) Mar 2026 330.213 → Sep 2026 336.940 (+2.037%)
semiannualInflation.source: BLS CPI-U NSA via FRED CPIAUCNS, updated 2026-11-10; computed in scenes/math.ts

inflationPart.unit: % inflation portion of the composite (composite − fixed), computed in scenes/math.ts; VO says 'about 4.1'

exampleInterest.unit: $ Illustrative: $10,000 × 5.51% ÷ 2, one six-month period (VO: 'about 275'); actual accrual is monthly and the rate resets in May 2027

minHold.unit: months before an I bond can be redeemed (31 CFR 359.6); redeemed before 5 years loses the last 3 months of interest (359.7)

notes: 5.51%/1.40% rest on secondary sources dated 2026-10-30 (TreasuryDirect blocked to automated access); the 2.04% inflation part and the 5.51% composite were recomputed from official CPI-U and the 31 CFR 359.14 formula and match.
The composite resets every six months; the inflation part can fall.
